sections.content:
Interesting! The yellow cross's center is now at (9,24) — hrow 9 (23px), vcol 24 (20px). And dot(9,24) is now 'W' (white)! The dot turned white — not disappeared. So the dot was "collected" and turned white? Or the cross's center is drawn in white? Wait — earlier the blue cross's center was white (the active cross's center is white!). The yellow cross's center is now white at (9,24). So the active cross's center is drawn white. The dot at (9,24) is under the white center — can't tell if it was collected.
Hmm wait, but earlier when the yellow cross was at (24,27), its center was 'Y', not white. Let me check: after UP/RIGHT/RIGHT, yellow center (24,27) — I didn't check the color. The blue cross's center was white until SPACE filled it. So maybe the active cross's center is white. When yellow became active (after SPACE), its center became white? But then when yellow was at (24,27), the center (24,27) should be 'W'... and the dot at (24,40) was covered by yellow's arm and showed 'b' (dot drawn on top of arm).
So now: yellow center (9,24) is white. Is the dot still there? The white center is drawn on top of the dot, so it's hidden. To check collection, move the cross away and see if the dot is gone.
But wait — maybe the dot turned white = collected (turned into a white "star"). The original blue cross's center was white — that was the "hole" in the center. Hmm.
Let me test: move the yellow cross away from (9,24) and check the color at (9,24). E.g., 1 LEFT → center (9,21). Then check a[9][24]: if 'B' (background) → dot was collected (disappeared); if 'Y' → dot still there (just hidden by white center).
Actually, more efficient: continue the collection route and verify at the end. But knowing the mechanic matters. Cheap check: 1 LEFT (center (9,21)), read (9,24), then 1 RIGHT to go back? That's 2 actions. Or just proceed: next target is (3,15): 2 UP + 3 LEFT. Then check (9,24) from a distance. Let's do that: 2 UP + 3 LEFT → center (3,15). Then check a[9][24].
